un_crc_intro.text: Under the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child 1989, which came into force in 1990, the following was approved:

hague_purpose.title: The purpose of this Convention is:
items: to secure the prompt return of children wrongfully removed or retained in any signatory state;
to effectively enforce in the other signatory states the rights of custody and visitation existing in a state that is signatory to the Convention.
hague_purpose.citation: Article 1 of the Hague Convention of 25 October 1980

seo.default_description: Information for parents dealing with international parental child abduction, wrongful removal or retention of a child in Poland, and Hague Convention return proceedings.

descriptions.introduction: Practical legal information on parental child abduction to or from Poland, Hague Convention child return cases, Polish courts, and urgent steps for parents.
descriptions.whom_to_contact: Find out which authorities, institutions and legal professionals to contact when a child has been wrongfully removed to or retained in Poland.
descriptions.jurisprudence: Selected case law on international parental child abduction, Hague Convention return proceedings and family law issues involving Poland.
descriptions.contact: Contact us about an urgent parental child abduction, wrongful retention or Hague Convention child return case involving Poland.
descriptions.who_we_are: Learn who is behind Poland Child Abduction and how legal assistance can support parents in cross-border child abduction cases involving Poland.
descriptions.privacy_policy: Read the privacy policy for Poland Child Abduction, including information about contact form data, personal information and website use.
descriptions.parental_child_abduction: Explanation of parental child abduction, wrongful removal and wrongful retention under the Hague Convention, with a focus on cases involving Poland.
descriptions.within_the_law: Overview of the international and national legal rules that may apply when a child is wrongfully removed to or retained in Poland.
descriptions.international_laws: International legal framework for parental child abduction cases, including the Hague Convention and cross-border child return procedures involving Poland.
descriptions.individual_national_laws: Guide to selected national laws that may affect international parental child abduction, custody and child return cases involving Poland.
descriptions.national_law_uk: Overview of British legal issues that may arise in international parental child abduction and child return cases involving Poland.
descriptions.national_law_us: Overview of American legal issues that may arise in international parental child abduction and child return cases involving Poland.
descriptions.national_law_canada: Overview of Canadian legal issues that may arise in international parental child abduction and child return cases involving Poland.
descriptions.national_law_poland: Overview of Polish legal rules relevant to custody, parental authority and international child abduction cases before Polish authorities and courts.
descriptions.what_should_i_do: First steps for a parent when a child has been taken to Poland or kept in Poland without consent, including documents, deadlines and legal options.
descriptions.steps_to_follow: Practical steps to take after a child has been wrongfully removed to or retained in Poland, including evidence, authorities and legal action.
descriptions.parents_in_contact: Guidance for parents who remain in contact and know the child or the other parent is in Poland, including negotiation, mediation and legal safeguards.
descriptions.parental_non_cooperation: Legal options when the other parent refuses mediation or cooperation after a child has been taken to or retained in Poland.
descriptions.conflict_with_the_other_parent: Information for parents in conflict about custody, travel, residence and international child abduction risks involving Poland.
descriptions.criminal_consequences: Overview of possible criminal consequences in international child abduction cases and why urgent legal advice is important when Poland is involved.
descriptions.why_remain_in_poland: Explanation of why a child and each parent may need to remain in Poland during family proceedings, mediation or Hague Convention child return cases.
descriptions.going_abroad_with_my_child: Information for parents considering international travel or relocation with a child, including consent, custody and child abduction risks involving Poland.
descriptions.is_it_possible: Can a parent go abroad with a child? Learn about consent, custody rights and legal limits before travel or relocation involving Poland.
descriptions.filial_relationship: Explanation of the parent-child relationship, parental authority and custody issues relevant to international travel and child abduction risks involving Poland.
descriptions.the_hague_convention: Guide to the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction and how child return proceedings work in Poland.
